class: A database role whose connection limit is smaller than the maximum a single application process's pool can open (plus any second process sharing the role) fails under load with 'too many connections' that surfaces as a 500 on whichever request needs a connection next, intermittently and only when several requests overlap.
mechanism: The ofo_app role has rolconnlimit 5; one API process's SQLAlchemy pool can grow to 15 (+ history); a second API process or a parallel e2e run on the same role exhausts the five slots.

first_seen.where: CI frontend e2e on PR #427, and a second API on :8766 on ofo_dev
first_seen.evidence: rolconnlimit 5 measured by a parallel session 2026-10-19 10:41; e2e failed 4/4 tries with asyncpg.exceptions.TooManyConnectionsError: too many connections for role "ofo_app" -> GET /strategies 500 -> saved-drafts list empty -> open-draft-3 click timeout (a re-run passed); the second API on :8766 hit it 11 times

fix: Not fixed. Class fix options (technical call): set the pool size and overflow below the role limit divided by the number of processes, and/or raise the role limit; a startup check that compares the pool maximum with rolconnlimit and refuses to start (or logs loudly) when it is higher.

detection.note: No test compares pool maximum with the role limit. Unmeasured: the production role's limit and the pool settings of the deployed process.
